mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -22.7 to -18.6 over the last three weeks, reflecting persistent reopening momentum; this momentum continues for four weeks and lifts the next 28-day mean above the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -22.7 at t-3w to -18.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to -20.3 (the last 28-day mean) despite three consecutive weekly increases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week rebound in WORKPLACES from -24.4 to -15.7 signals returning commuting and office activity, which raises weekday retail-and-recreation footfall over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 8 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -24.4 at t-1w to -15.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: After a >8 point weekly rise in WORKPLACES, the mean RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is lower than over the prior 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT is above -30 and WORKPLACES is above -20, transit use and office presence reinforce each other, increasing trips that pass through retail-and-recreation venues; the interaction produces higher RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -29.3 and WORKPLACES is -15.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: When both thresholds are met, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In the late-autumn cold-weather regime, negative PARKS values indicate outdoor recreation is suppressed, shifting recreation demand indoors toward retail-and-recreation venues over the next week.
failure_condition: In weeks with PARKS below -5 during late autumn, the following 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than or equal to the prior 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM remains above +2.0, indicating essential-trip priority and pandemic caution, which crowds out discretionary retail-and-recreation trips over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM is above +2.0, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is higher than the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS is negative and falling in November due to seasonal cooling, which historically coincides with a shift of recreation spending to indoor retail; this seasonal substitution raises RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS negative in all four snapshot weeks
failure_condition: Across late-autumn periods with negative PARKS, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A divergence where TRANSIT stays deeply negative (< -25) while WORKPLACES recovers (> -20) indicates commuters avoid transit but return to offices, boosting retail near workplaces; the interaction raises RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: When TRANSIT < -25 and WORKPLACES > -20, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a restriction-tightening regime, RESIDENTIAL above +15 signals residents staying home and avoiding retail venues; this behavioral response lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Under restriction-tightening, when RESIDENTIAL > 15, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not lower than the last 28-day mean.
